title: Weight provenance adapter and version stamping runner
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Build a standalone adapter and runner that accepts external OSS weights, records cryptographic provenance, converts to canonical runtime formats, executes deterministic validation and micro-smoke runs, and emits a version-stamp (canonical pin) plus a first-pass performance profile for publishing. This ticket scopes the end-to-end flow for the intake sentinel: manifest verification, signed checksum validation, provenance metadata enrichment, format normalization (safetensors/torch->runtime artifact), reproducible fingerprinting, pin stamping, and profile emitter to the catalog service.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter can accept and validate manifests with signature and checksum and reject tampered uploads
Conversion produces runtime-compatible artifact with identical model outputs for reference prompts (within tolerance)
Version-stamp (pin) is generated deterministically and recorded in catalog with provenance metadata
A baseline performance profile (latency P50/P95, token cost estimate, memory footprint) is emitted to profiles endpoint
End-to-end flow runs in sandbox and produces audit log suitable for manual review
steps_taken: Spike: implemented prototype manifest verifier using ed25519 and SHA-256 (internal repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proofs PR #312)
Validated conversion path for a 7B decoder-only model from safetensors -> runtime tar (script: tools/convert_canonical.sh)
Added deterministic seed and canonical tokenization checks to conversion to minimize nondeterminism
Created lightweight micro-smoke harness that runs 5 canonical prompts and records token-wise outputs and timing
decisions: Chosen to implement a separate 'provenance-adapter' microservice instead of extending artifact-gateway to keep blast radius small
Store pin as semantic SHA256 prefix + human-readable metadata instead of monotonic numeric IDs to preserve reproducibility
Initial performance profiles will be synthetic: cached prefix caching disabled and short-seq latency measurement; later work will add workload-based profiling
Opted for safetensors-first conversion path as primary canonical format; torch fallback supported for older artifacts
tradeoffs_and_risks: Running deterministic validations increases intake latency (adds ~30-90s). To mitigate, we perform fast-path acceptance with post-acceptance certification in parallel
True production-quality profiling requires load testing and KV-cache warmup; initial profiles will under-estimate steady-state throughput
Security: accepting external signed manifests requires a revocation list and signer onboarding process that needs operations support
qa_and_validation: Integration test run ID: intg-2025-02-03-07 (passed 18/20 checks; two non-blocking tokenizer mismatch warnings)
Determinism suite: ran across three seeds and two hardware backends (A100, T4) with tolerance thresholds recorded
Canary sandbox runs scheduled on 2025-02-10 to validate real-world ingest at 5rps
notes_and_next_steps: Finish signer revocation API and integrate with security team for onboarding policy
Wire up profile emitter to console-profiles ingestion endpoint and add dashboard card for new-model traffic
Add post-acceptance background job to run full quantization and extended regression evals
Coordinate with PM (Rosa Malik) to draft customer communication for newly cataloged community models
